name: Type Ia supernovae as standard candles
summary: Type Ia light curves, standardised by width-luminosity corrections, give luminosity distances that revealed cosmic acceleration; stellar explosion physics sets the systematics of the dark-energy inference.

name: Galaxy bias links halos to the matter field
summary: Galaxy surveys trace the cosmic web only through galaxy formation physics; halo occupation and bias connect observed clustering to the underlying matter power spectrum.

name: Lensing maps dark matter
summary: Lensing responds to total mass irrespective of luminosity, so strong and weak lensing give direct mass maps and halo profiles, as in the Bullet Cluster and subhalo searches.

name: CMB acoustic peaks require non-baryonic matter
summary: Relative heights of the acoustic peaks fix the baryon and total matter densities; the third peak demands collisionless dark matter that decoupled potentials from the photon-baryon fluid.

name: Cluster dynamics, gas and lensing mass
summary: Zwicky's virial argument, X-ray hydrostatic gas masses and lensing all show clusters dominated by dark matter, and the Bullet Cluster separates the mass from the baryons.

name: Lensing probes dark subhalos
summary: Flux-ratio anomalies and gravitational imaging of strong lenses detect low-mass subhalos, constraining warm, fuzzy and self-interacting dark matter on sub-galactic scales.

name: Baryonic feedback vs dark-matter physics
summary: Cusp-core, missing satellites and too-big-to-fail can be solved either by new dark-matter physics or by supernova feedback and reionization suppressing dwarf galaxy formation; the two are degenerate.

name: Cosmic-ray backgrounds for dark-matter signals
summary: Antiprotons, positrons and gamma rays from dark-matter annihilation must be separated from astrophysical cosmic-ray production and propagation, as in the positron excess and antiproton debates.

name: Hierarchical growth from primordial perturbations
summary: Gravitational growth of primordial density perturbations builds halos, filaments and then galaxies; large-scale structure statistics supply the initial conditions for galaxy formation.

name: Dark halos host galaxies
summary: Galaxies form within dark-matter halos, whose potentials set rotation curves, scaling relations and merger histories.

name: AGN as neutrino sources
summary: Blazars such as TXS 0506+056 and Seyferts like NGC 1068 are identified IceCube sources; hadronic acceleration in jets and coronae produces neutrinos with gamma rays.

name: Clusters as dark-matter laboratories
summary: Cluster mass budgets from X-ray hydrostatic equilibrium, SZ, lensing and galaxy velocities give dark-matter fractions and collisional constraints.

name: Dwarf galaxy tests of CDM
summary: Dwarf galaxy scaling relations and simulations are the testing ground for CDM versus alternatives, with baryonic physics the key systematic.

name: Reionization imprinted on the CMB
summary: Thomson scattering from free electrons after reionization gives the optical depth tau and large-angle E-mode polarization bump, plus kinetic SZ, constraining when first galaxies ionized the universe.

name: Galactic dynamics and the local halo
summary: Milky Way rotation curve, Gaia stellar streams and escape velocity measure the halo mass and local density, key inputs to direct-detection rates.

name: Magnetars as FRB engines
summary: The Galactic magnetar SGR 1935+2154 emitted an FRB-like burst, tying FRBs to highly magnetised neutron stars.

name: Microlensing finds planets
summary: Gravitational microlensing, developed for MACHO searches, detects cold and free-floating planets beyond the reach of transits and radial velocity.

name: Stellar populations as galactic archaeology
summary: Ages, abundances and kinematics of stellar populations, with Gaia, reconstruct the Milky Way's assembly history and star-formation history.

name: Supernova systematics in the dark-energy era
summary: Progenitor, host-galaxy and dust effects on Type Ia luminosities limit precision on the dark-energy equation of state, relevant to DESI and Rubin-era samples.

name: CMB tests inflationary predictions
summary: Near scale-invariant adiabatic Gaussian fluctuations, the spectral tilt and limits on tensor modes from B-mode polarization constrain inflationary models.

name: Acoustic oscillations as standard ruler
summary: The same sound horizon at the drag epoch imprinted in the CMB peaks appears as the BAO feature in galaxy clustering, giving a standard ruler across redshift.

name: Distance ladder and Hubble tension
summary: Cepheid and TRGB calibrated Type Ia supernovae set the local H0 that disagrees with CMB inference; stellar physics systematics are central to the dispute.

name: Time-delay cosmography and cosmic shear
summary: Strong-lens time delays give H0 independent of the distance ladder, while weak-lensing shear measures S8, the other tension.

name: BAO and DESI dark-energy constraints
summary: BAO distances combined with supernovae and CMB constrain the dark-energy equation of state; DESI hints at evolving w.

name: Dark matter in the Friedmann budget
summary: Evidence from CMB, BBN and structure growth fixes the cold dark matter density parameter in the Friedmann equation that sets expansion history.

name: Galaxy scaling relations and MOND
summary: Baryonic Tully-Fisher and the radial acceleration relation are tight galaxy scaling laws that MOND predicts directly, whereas CDM must reproduce them through feedback.

name: Cluster problem for MOND
summary: MOND fits rotation curves but needs extra unseen mass in clusters, and the Bullet Cluster lensing offset challenges it.
breaks: Fails at cluster scales without additional dark components such as sterile neutrinos.

name: Short GRBs from neutron-star mergers
summary: GW170817 with GRB 170817A and the kilonova established compact mergers as short-GRB progenitors, with off-axis jet physics.

name: Gravitational waves from compact binaries
summary: Neutron-star and black-hole mergers are the gravitational-wave sources; kilonovae probe r-process nucleosynthesis and dense-matter equation of state.

name: Long GRBs and collapsars
summary: Long GRBs accompany broad-lined Type Ic supernovae from collapsing massive stars, linking relativistic jets to core-collapse explosions.

name: Supernova remnants accelerate cosmic rays
summary: Diffusive shock acceleration at supernova remnant shocks is the standard origin of Galactic cosmic rays up to the knee.

name: Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect
summary: Inverse-Compton scattering of CMB photons by hot intracluster electrons distorts the CMB spectrum, yielding cluster catalogs and pressure profiles.

name: Solar neutrinos and neutrino astronomy
summary: Solar neutrino detection, resolving the solar neutrino problem via oscillations, established the techniques and flavor physics later used in astrophysical neutrino telescopes.

name: Degeneracy pressure sets remnant masses
summary: Stellar evolution ends in white dwarfs, neutron stars or black holes, and degeneracy pressure support yields the Chandrasekhar and TOV mass limits.

name: Disks around young stars and accretion
summary: Viscous accretion disks govern protoplanetary evolution and mass transfer in binaries, sharing alpha-disk transport and angular-momentum redistribution.
breaks: Protoplanetary disks are cool, dusty and partly neutral, so non-ideal MHD and dust dynamics differ from ionized binary disks.

name: Accretion disk theory shared
summary: Shakura-Sunyaev alpha disks and MRI-driven turbulence describe both AGN accretion and protoplanetary disks.
breaks: Disk temperature, ionization and radiation pressure regimes differ by many orders of magnitude, so MRI activity and dead zones apply differently.

name: Radiative transfer in atmospheres
summary: Exoplanet atmosphere retrievals use radiative transfer and opacities developed for stellar atmospheres, and stellar activity and limb darkening contaminate transmission spectra.
